datasets_evaluated.evidence: In the experiment focused on comparative analysis of malicious encrypted traffic detection, we employ CICIDS2017, MalwareTraffic-Analysis.net, StratosphereIPS, and USTC-TFC2016—for both model training and validation purposes.

label_source.evidence: The annotated flow records encompass essential details such as timestamps, source and destination IP addresses, ports, protocols, and indications of malicious activity.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: this approach leverages both traffic-level and packet-level data of encrypted traffic to automate feature extraction and comprehensively learn the behavioral and temporal characteristics of traffic data

ech_considered.evidence: The encryption of traffic, while safeguarding data confidentiality, also provides convenience for attackers to conceal malicious activities.

model_family.evidence: Secondly, a dual layer bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network which is supervised is employed to model packet-level data in encrypted traffic, capturing local semantic features (temporal features) of each packet-level data.

split_protocols.evidence: The dataset is split into a training set and a test set in an 8:2 ratio and undergoes ten-fold cross-validation.

shortcut_check.evidence: In this paper, since we propose multiple modules, we set up a set of ablation experiments to judge the contribution of each module.

metrics.evidence: we evaluate its performance using four metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

granularity.evidence: The original PCAP files are split into individual traffic data using the SplitCap tool, and packet-level data with the same traffic feature quintuples are merged into a single traffic data.

first_n_packets.evidence: Since the first 8 data packets of the traffic typically contain complete handshake information [46], N is set to 8 in this paper.
